scope: Final four-pass review of the bounded native right-hand closed-grip refinement candidate

issues.title: Pinky distal support remains open while new Ring-Pinky self-crossings are introduced

evidence.crossing_localization: Ring2-to-Pinky2, with one Pinky1-involved pair; not the unsupported Pinky3 tip

issues.impact: The three actual 0.3 m views show a substantially tighter grip overall, but the distal little finger remains visibly unsupported. The added Ring-Pinky crossings show that the bounded extra curl displaced another part of the finger band rather than completing clean support.
issues.required_fix: Before final grip acceptance, diagnose the Ring2/Pinky2 and Pinky1 crossing band separately from the unsupported Pinky3 tip, then refine only the relevant closed rotations against the same actual surface and self-contact constraints. Reverting the extra Pinky3 flex alone does not remove the ten crossings. Preserve the accepted thumb retreat/press, open row, wrist/Grip/root and all non-pose data. Do not optimize raw pair count at the expense of visible support.

evidence: The original BIN prefix, geometry, UV, skin, IBM, materials, three KTX payloads, root, wrist, Grip, bone lengths and all non-pose JSON/accessors remain exact.

All 15 open time-0 finger rows are byte-identical. Only nine right-finger closed rows and corresponding default rotations change; default equals grip time 1, and the post-delta quaternion application error is below 2.66e-8 chord distance.

Nonfinger and left-bone matrices, unaffected skinned vertices and cuff-cap skinning remain unchanged at open, mid and closed samples. Negative contract tests reject wrist translation, open-row mutation and KTX mutation.

On the identical 7167 samples, whole-hand inside samples fall from 277 to 2 and maximum signed-core penetration magnitude falls from 11.48591 mm to 0.092522 mm. Samples deeper than the provisional 0.25 mm working cutoff fall from 256 to zero.

Thumb, Mid, Ring and Pinky sampled solid-core penetration all fall to zero. The two remaining shallow samples belong to unchanged Index3 and are retained as actual negative signed values rather than rounded to strict zero.
Thumb3-to-Index nearest actual surface distance improves from 0.084871 mm to 0.043760 mm, with samples within 1 mm increasing from 23 to 24; this supports the visible opposing thumb press.
Position-weld interpretation improves Thumb-Index nonadjacent crossings from 50 to 47 and Mid-Ring from 64 to 62, but Ring-Pinky regresses from zero to ten and Pinky3 loses nearby support.
The front, back and thumb-side oblique images are actual 0.3 m renders from the candidate KTX pixels and formal dao with identity roots and no material override or model rescale.

Compared with the native terminal/source default, the formerly long straight finger silhouette is visibly pulled back into a more compact wrap. The front view reads as a closed grasp rather than fingers laid along the shaft.
The thumb-side and back views show a credible opposing thumb/palm clamp and no renewed handle-core breakthrough, wrist drift or cuff regression.

The oblique view still exposes separation around the little-finger distal band, consistent with the measured lack of cord or Ring support; therefore the visible improvement is real but not final-quality complete.
No model rebuild, SDK, application, HTML, Kotlin, formal/shared producer, device, Gradle or Git path is changed by this private candidate.
The candidate reuses a bounded previously measured retreat correction and one bounded Pinky3 flexion; no parameter grid or speculative animation system is introduced.

limits: The finite vertex, edge-midpoint and face-centroid samples do not prove a continuous maximum on the nonconvex handle core.
The 0.25 mm value is a provisional art-session working decision cutoff, not measurement precision or permission to claim strict zero penetration.

This review approves a bounded visible first-piece handoff to Root native review only. It does not approve formal publication, PICO SDK behavior, device input, runtime rendering or final grip quality.
